requirements.evidence: Every contract item is implemented: the migrations with named indexes and the stored owner_seq column (create_entity_memberships_table.php:16-24); the models, enum and factories; both policies (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php); pick with Gate::authorize, an audit log line and a redirect (EntityController.php:15-28); and the routes with auth+verified (routes/web.php:30-36). Members covers duplicate -> email error, Rule::in(manageable), owner/last-manager 403 (Members.php:42-96). Settings covers the slug unique-ignore rule, delete with membership removal and session clearing, and a transactional transfer with admin-of-this-entity and vanished-owner 403 (Settings.php:46-100). Lang keys exist in both locales and docs/database-schema.md is updated.

conventions.evidence: The conventions say domain writes go through app/Actions/*, but every write is inline in the components: Members.php:48 `memberships()->create`, :75 `$membership->update`, :96 `delete()`, and Settings.php:46,55-56,98-99. Settings validates through `rules()` (Settings.php:107) instead of the project's #[Validate] pattern, and `$targetMembershipId` has no validation rule at all. Policies, $fillable via #[Fillable], Bulma, Blade components (x-form-field, x-button), the CHANGELOG and the docs all follow the conventions.

security.evidence: Every public action authorizes on the server. Membership IDs are resolved and scoped to the locked entity before authorize (Members.php:58-64, 80-86). Settings re-authorizes in each action, and transfer looks up its target under `whereKey(...)->where('role', Admin)` inside the entity with lockForUpdate. `public Entity $entity` is #[Locked] and output is escaped with {{ }}. A small gap: `public mixed $targetMembershipId` (Settings.php:28) has no #[Validate] or rules entry; filter_var + abort(403) cover it instead.

tests.evidence: Pest suites cover the models/DB constraints (EntityModelTest.php), the policies, pick including session-untouched on 403 and the audit log mock, the dashboard settings-URL hiding and session-pointing-elsewhere 403, and Members unauthorized and tampered-ID calls (EntityMembersTest.php:1546-1561). Settings has a locked-entity tamper test and several transfer failure paths. Missing: no direct unauthorized-call test of the Settings save/delete/transfer actions (only the mount 403 is tested), and the last-manager test uses an artificial entity with no owner.

simplicity.evidence: The code is lean overall and reuses existing Blade components and the policies. One duplication: the role-check helper `isManager` is copy-pasted in both policies (EntityPolicy.php:720-725 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:657-662), and the same entity-scoping check `(int) $membership->entity_id !== (int) $this->entity->getKey()` is duplicated in Members.php.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods short, with PHPDoc on the policies and relations and no dead code. Small nits: fully qualified `\App\Models\UserRole::Owner` is repeated inline in members.blade.php, and the members role select offers an 'owner' option (members.blade.php:1121) that the server always rejects.

scope.evidence: The diff adds `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml` (a deploy pipeline using HOSTINGER_API/PF_GIT_TOKEN secrets) and `.github/workflows/tests.yml`. Neither is related to the entities task. Everything else serves the task.

issues.explanation: These new CI/deploy workflows, including a deploy job that uses production secrets, are unrelated to the entities task and should not ship in this PR.
The conventions require domain writes (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) to go through app/Actions/* classes, but these writes are inline in the Livewire components.
Public property `$targetMembershipId` is typed `mixed` and has no #[Validate] rule, against Livewire policy rule 1; filter_var/abort only partly compensates.
name/slug are validated through a rules() method rather than the project's #[Validate] attribute pattern used in Members.
No test calls save/delete/transfer as a non-owner at the action level (for example after the role changes post-mount); only the mount 403 is covered.
The role select offers 'owner' for non-owner rows; choosing it always produces a validation error, so the option should only be rendered for the owner row.
The isManager role check is duplicated in both policies.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model, policies, pick endpoint and the Dashboard/Members/Settings Livewire pages correctly and securely, with thorough Pest coverage and updated docs. It is held back by two unrelated GitHub workflow files (including a deploy pipeline) and by domain writes made inline in the components instead of through app/Actions, so it needs changes before merging.
